## Overview

One player is the Chancellor; the others are Exiles or Citizens. Players compete for a changing Oath, personal Visions, or succession to the Chancellor. One player wins alone. After victory, the winner writes the Chronicle, preserving a changed map, population of cards, and political order for the next game. New players can join later games.

This summary covers the complete multiplayer base game, first-game and later-game setup, and Chronicle. It incorporates the official first-printing clarifications, particularly the corrected Darkest Secret recovery restriction and Imperial defense sharing. A player's pawn determines **your site** and **your region**. A pawn does not rule a site, and warbands on your board do not garrison its site. Even one of your warbands physically on a faceup site is sufficient to rule it, regardless of where your pawn is. You rule each faceup site containing your warbands, the cards at those sites, and your advisers. Moving a pawn by itself leaves site garrisons and their rule unchanged. Sites hold only one color of warbands; different colors cannot coexist there to share rule. All Imperial players rule every purple-garrisoned site. Bandits rule faceup sites without physical warbands; they are enemies to all players and do not compete for victory. Facedown sites cannot hold cards or be ruled.
